values: Respect for humanity and the environment
Honesty, upholding and defending the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

themes.theme_description: This unit integrates four Advanced Level existing History units including National Movements and New States in Africa Since 1935, Social and Economic History of East Africa Since 1800, Theory of Government and Constitutional Development and Practice in East Africa, and History of Africa 1855–1914.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the influence of the Pan-African movement on the liberation of Blacks to appreciate the need for a united and developed Africa.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the origins of Pan-Africanism, its key events and figures to appreciate their contribution to the foundation of African independence struggles. (k, u, v)
evaluate the factors for the rise of Pan-Africanism to understand its impact on the need for African freedom, equality and a fair world. (gs, v, a)
analyse the challenges to the growth of Pan-Africanism to appreciate the challenges of modern African states. (gs, v, a)
examine the impact of Pan-Africanism to appreciate its role in promoting unity, independence and social justice across Africa and beyond. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Individually, learners use textbooks and internet sources to investigate the origins, objectives and key personalities of Pan-Africanism.
Learners, in groups, use an extract about Pan-Africanism to find out the factors that led to the rise of Pan-Africanism and present their findings to class. Teacher does a wrap-up.
In groups, learners analyse any two case studies outside East Africa on how specific African countries have struggled since the 20th century to implement the ideals of Pan-Africanism.
Learners in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present the challenges being faced by Pan-Africanism.
Learners write an essay on how the rise of Pan-Africanism has impacted the global world in the aspects of freedom, equality and justice.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ ability to analyse factors that contributed to the rise of Pan-Africanism and take note of their ability to: i) write and present coherently. ii) work effectively in diverse teams.

Converse with learners to assess their understanding of the challenges faced by Pan-Africanists during the post-colonial era in Africa and take note of: i) their eloquence. ii) their respect for one another. iii) how they consult one another.
Evaluate learners’ ability to sort and analyse the activities of Pan-Africanism and their contributions to Africa’s independence in the aspects of justice, freedom and equality.

suggested_uses: Use internet sources to investigate the origins, objectives and key personalities of Pan-Africanism.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 2: Post-Colonial Socio-Economic Developments in East Africa

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of post-colonial socio-economic developments in Africa by examining the trade unions and the cooperative movement in East Africa to appreciate the need to address workers’ welfare and promote development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the evolution of trade unions to understand the beginning of worker’s organisations in Uganda. (u,v, a)
evaluate the role of trade unions in East Africa to appreciate their contribution to the fight for workers’ rights. (gs, v, a)
analyse the history of the cooperative movement in East Africa to understand the beginning of farmer’s collective efforts to uplift themselves in East Africa. (gs,v, a)
examine the role of the cooperative movement in East Africa to understand the region’s economic development and social change. (gs, v, a)
analyse the challenges faced by trade unions and the cooperative movement in East Africa by 1985 to appreciate how best trade unions and the cooperative movement can be managed today in East Africa.

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners collaboratively explore the concept of “trade union” and give examples such as: Uganda Railway Workers Union (URWU), the National Organisation of Trade Unions (NOTU), Uganda National Teachers’ Union (UNATU) and Tanganyika Federation of Labour (TFL), among others, through questioning and discussion.
Learners use textbooks, magazines and internet sources to investigate the evolution of trade union movement in East Africa.
Learners, in a brainstorming session, discuss and present the key objectives of trade unions in East Africa and the teacher does a wrap-up.
Learners search, using textbooks, extracts or the internet, to find out the role of trade unions in Uganda.
Learners, in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present the role of trade unions in advocating for the rights of workers in East Africa and the teacher does a wrap-up.

Learners collaboratively explore the concept of “cooperative movement” and give examples such as Bugisu Cooperative Union, Banyankole-Kweterana Cooperative Union, and East Mengo Cooperative Union, among others, through questioning and discussion.
Learners use textbooks, magazines and the internet sources to investigate the evolution of the cooperative movement in East Africa.
Learners, in a brainstorming session, discuss and present the key objectives of cooperative movements in East Africa.
In groups, learners search, using sources like textbooks and the internet, for the role of cooperative societies in the socio-economic development of East Africa.
Learners work, in groups, to explore strategies used by cooperative unions to empower communities today.
Learners, in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present the challenges of any one cooperative movement in Uganda today.
Learners, in a debate session, discuss the results of the establishment of cooperative movements in East Africa.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners during a class discussion to assess their ability to explain the role of trade union movements in East Africa and take note of their ability to: i) respect one another. ii) use accurate facts. iii) use proper timelines.

Dialogue with learners in a discussion to assess their ability to analyse the impact of cooperative movements during the debate and take note of their: i) comprehension of facts. ii) level of teamwork.
Assess learners’ relevance and accuracy of facts during the presentation on the strategies used to empower cooperative members in our communities today.

suggested_uses: Use internet sources to investigate the evolution of trade union movement in East Africa.
Use internet sources to investigate the evolution of the cooperative movement in East Africa.
Use internet sources to search for the role of cooperative societies.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 3: Regional Economic Groupings and International Relations

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the need to address common challenges by analysing the activities of selected regional organisations and economic groupings to appreciate regional integration in Africa.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to understand its role in promoting the sovereignty and independence of member states. (gs v, a)
assess the role of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) to appreciate its impact on regional trade and economic integration among member states. (gs, v, a)
analyse the role of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) to understand its role in promoting regional trade and economic integration in contemporary Africa.(gs, v, a)
evaluate the role of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU) to appreciate its contribution to fostering regional trade, economic integration and development among its member states. (v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In a think-pair-share session, learners use diverse resources such as textbooks, extracts, newspaper articles, magazines and the internet to research the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM). They summarise key ideas on its composition, origins, principles and roles, focusing on its influence on global politics during and after the Cold War.
Learners compare the strategies of the NAM with those founded on the grounds of socialism and capitalism.

In groups, learners carry out a search on the origin, aims, and achievements of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) using textbooks, magazines, the internet, and other credible sources.

Learners analyse a case study of a COMESA-led project or initiative, focusing on its impact on regional economic integration and development. They present their analysis in a structured format, such as a report or presentation, and facilitate a class discussion on the project’s implications.
In groups, using textbooks and other internet sources, learners investigate the origin, aims and achievements of the formation of Southern African Development Community (SADC).
In groups, learners analyse a specific SADC development initiative, such as the North-South Corridor, and assess its impact on member states.

Learners design a short documentary showcasing one SADC-led project or initiative. The documentary should highlight the project’s goals, implementation and impact on regional economic integration and development.

Learners collaborate, in groups, to explore the origin, aims and achievements of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU) using textbooks, magazines, the internet, and other resources. Each group presents their findings in a creative format, such as role-play, a poster or a digital presentation.
Learners analyse a specific AMU-led project or initiative, examining its impact on regional economic integration and development. Their findings are shared through an interactive presentation.

Learners compare the strategies and initiatives of the AMU with those of another African economic community. The comparison focuses on the strategies used to enhance regional integration, and learners present their analysis in structured debates or comparative reports.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they present the role of NAM and assess their ability to communicate effectively using relevant historical data and good listening skills.

Converse with learners to assess their ability to explain the contributions of SADC to the socio-economic and political development of central African states and take note of their: i) confidence. ii) interactivity and teamwork.
Evaluate the relevance, accuracy and coherence of learners’ write-ups on the impact of COMESA on regional trade and economic integration.
Assess learners’ ability to work individually or collaboratively in identifying the roles of SADC in the development of southern African states.

suggested_uses: Use internet to research the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM).
Carry out a search on COMESA using the internet.
Use internet sources to investigate SADC.
Use internet to explore AMU.

themes.theme_title: Unit 2: History of World Affairs Since 1789
themes.theme_description: This unit combines content from the following two existing Advanced Level History units: European History of 1789–1970 and World Affairs Since 1939.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the interests of major powers in the Balkans by analysing the conflicts in Eastern Europe to appreciate how foreign interests can result in conflicts.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the factors behind the rise of the Ottoman Empire and its impact on Europe to understand the challenges related to state formation and consolidation. (k, gs, v, a)
examine the challenges posed by the 1831–1841 Syrian Question on Europe to understand how conflicting foreign interests can hinder the building of peaceful nations. (v, a)
analyse the causes of the 1854–1856 Crimean War and its impact on Europe to understand the current geopolitical conflicts and alliances in the world. (v, a)
assess the impact of the 1878 Congress of Berlin on settling European disputes and its relevance to modern diplomatic resolutions in Africa. (v, a)
evaluate the impact of the 1908–1913 Balkan Crisis on Europe to appreciate the need for unity, patriotism and nationalism. (v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, in class, use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to research the factors that led to the rise and expansion of the Ottoman Empire.
Learners, in a debate session, discuss the impact of the growth and expansion of the Ottoman Empire on the growth of Europe.
Learners, in a jigsaw session, share ideas on the 1831–1841 Syrian Question, focusing on the background, causes, course and impact.
Learners, in a learning station session, share and discuss the background, causes, course and effects of the 1854–1856 Crimean War.
Learners, in a debate session, discuss the significance of the 1856 Paris Peace Treaty that concluded the Crimean War.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks or other sources to find out the events that led to the 1878 Berlin Congress, its terms and significance for Europe and Asia.
Learners, in groups, use textbooks, history extracts and other sources to find out the causes and impacts of the 1908–1913 Balkan Crisis on Europe.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss factors for the rise and expansion of the Ottoman Empire and take note of their ability to: i) collaborate positively with team members. ii) sort and analyse issues clearly. iii) talk confidently and explain issues clearly.
Converse with learners as they discuss the impact of the 1856 Crimean War and assess their ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams. ii) evaluate different situations.
Assess the relevance, accuracy and coherence of the learners’ write-up on the terms of the 1878 Berlin Congress in providing peace in Europe.

suggested_uses: Use internet to research the rise and expansion of the Ottoman Empire.
Use internet to find out events leading to the 1878 Berlin Congress.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 2: World War I and its Aftermath

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses one of the international conflicts by evaluating the causes and effects of World War I to appreciate how the war has shaped world order since 1918.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the causes and results of the 1914–1918 World War I and its relevance to contemporary conflict prevention and international relations. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the role of the Versailles Peace Treaty of 1919 to understand its impact on Europe and international diplomacy. (gs, v, a)
analyse the role of the 1920–1939 League of Nations in maintaining world peace to promote the workings of international diplomacy. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the causes and impact of the 1929–1935 World Economic Depression to understand how bad economic policies can result in economic crises. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, in a think-pair-share session, interact on the concept of World War I by focusing on its origin and major events leading to the war.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks and other reading materials to search and present on the causes of World War I of 1914–1918.
Learners, in learning stations, discuss and present the reasons for the defeat of the Central Powers.
Learners, in a brainstorming session, discuss the effects of World War I and its role in shaping international relations.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks or other sources to search for the Treaty of Versailles, focusing on its terms and the extent to which it contributed to peace in Europe.
Learners, in groups, write essays evaluating the successes and shortcomings of the Versailles Peace Treaty.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks and history extracts to search for the objectives and founding members of the League of Nations.
Learners, in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present the challenges faced by the League of Nations.
Learners, in a debate session, discuss how the League of Nations was an instrument of peace after World War I. The teacher does a wrap-up.
Learners, in pairs, discuss and present the concept of the World Economic Depression of 1929–35.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks and other sources to explore the causes and results of the World Economic Depression.
Learners, in groups, brainstorm strategies adopted by European powers to overcome the challenges of the World Economic Depression of 1929–35.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learners’ ability to interact effectively with others as they discuss the factors that led to the outbreak of World War I.
Converse with learners to assess their confidence as they present the terms of the 1919 Versailles Peace Treaty.
Analyse learners’ ability to take notes and record accurate and coherent ideas during the debate on the effectiveness of the League of Nations in maintaining world peace.
Evaluate the relevance and accuracy of the consequences of the 1929–1935 World Economic Depression presented by the learners.

suggested_uses: Use internet to search and present on the causes of World War I.
Use internet to search for the Treaty of Versailles.
Use internet to search for the objectives and founding members of the League of Nations.
Use internet to explore the causes and results of the World Economic Depression.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 4: Sovereignty and Constitutionalism in East Africa

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the concepts of sovereignty and constitutionalism by examining the role of parliament, the press and media to appreciate their contribution to democracy, good governance and respect for human rights in East Africa.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the concepts of sovereignty and constitutionalism to understand their rights, responsibilities and their limits. (gs, v, a)
explain how parliament represents the will of the people and reflects their voice in decision-making to promote inclusive governance. (v, a)
analyse the representation and respect of the rights of minority groups in parliament so as to appreciate the need to respect the rights of others.(v, a)
analyse the role of the press and media in the constitutional development of East Africa to appreciate its role in promoting good governance. (v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners read and analyse texts or watch videos about sovereignty. They summarise key ideas about its meaning, key aspects (components), characteristics, and how it relates to laws and personal actions.
Each group creates a schematic chart to illustrate the ideas they have summarised and their interrelationships. The charts are displayed in the classroom for peer critique and constructive feedback.
Learners discuss how parliament represents the will of the people, providing specific examples of how parliamentary decisions impact citizens’ lives.

Learners view video documentaries or story narrations by a guest speaker on various parliament systems worldwide to understand how they represent their people and interests. This is followed by a teacher’s wrap-up and a guided discussion analysing the roles and functions of parliamentary systems and governance.
Learners role-play a parliamentary session, debating and voting on a key policy related to democracy and governance in Africa
Learners use textbooks, newspapers, ICT tools and other sources to search for the roles of different special minority groups in Uganda’s parliament.
Learners role-play as members of special minority groups in parliament, debating a current issue to explore how these groups influence legislative decisions.
Learners brainstorm and list the various forms of media used in Uganda, discussing their unique roles and significance.

Learners conduct a search on and investigate the role of the media in Africa’s constitutional development, analysing its impact on public opinion, political participation, and the promotion of democratic values.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners during class discussion to assess their ability to work positively with their peers, listening attentively while sharing the concept of sovereignty.

Engage in a dialogue with learners and assess their ability to explain the structure and operations of parliament. Focus assessment on: i) eloquence of the voice used. ii) respect for historical timelines. iii) willingness to work in teams.
Evaluate the relevance, accuracy and coherence of learners’ write-ups examining the role of special minority groups in parliament.
Evaluate learners’ relevance, accuracy and coherence of facts while explaining the role of the media in the constitutional development of Africa.

suggested_uses: Use ICT tools to search for the roles of different special minority groups in Uganda’s parliament.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 5: Post- Independence Ideologies in East Africa

topics.core_competency: The learner evaluates the efforts of the early post-independence leaders by examining the ideologies they adopted to appreciate their contribution to the transformation of people.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse Nyerere’s Ujamaa policy to appreciate its contribution to the rural development initiative, unity and patriotism. (gs, v, a)
evaluate Kenyatta’s Harambee philosophy to appreciate the need for self-reliance strategies for growth and development. (gs, v, a)
examine the activities of Asians in post-colonial East Africa to appreciate the value of inclusivity as well as their contribution to the development of East Africa. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, in pairs, use textbooks, internet sources and other reading materials to analyse the concept of “Ujamaa villages”, and photographs of rural communities working together to explain the functions of the policy, note down their findings, make presentations, and provide feedback on each pairs’ work.
Learners discuss examples of communities in their localities or other parts of Uganda that apply ideas similar to those of Ujamaa and explore possible reasons for such practices.
Learners use textbooks or extracts on Ujamaa to investigate the origin, principles, goals and developmental impact of the Ujamaa policy in Tanzania.

Learners study a teacher-provided textbook or digital map showing the distribution of Ujamaa villages in Tanzania. They select specific examples of Ujamaa villages (e.g. Matondombiri) to research the methods used to implement the Ujamaa policy, its successes and challenges in improving rural community life.
Learners brainstorm the meaning and evolution of Kenya’s Harambee philosophy.
In groups, learners create a journal outlining the key principles, goals and socio-economic impacts of the Harambee philosophy in Kenya.
Learners develop a journal showcasing the contributions of Asians in Ugandan communities through a variety of activities.

Learners use textbooks, newspapers, ICT tools and other sources to study the history of Asian communities in Uganda. They identify the challenges faced by these communities in implementing their activities.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they write and present coherent explanations of the impact of the Ujamaa policy on Tanzania’s development.

Engage learners in a dialogue to assess their ability to organise and analyse historical information on the socio-economic impact of the Harambee philosophy in Kenya. Focus assessment on their ability to listen attentively and demonstrate comprehension.
Assess learners’ ability to present relevant, accurate and coherent facts on the Asian contributions to the development of East Africa, highlighting their analysis and critical thinking skills.

suggested_uses: Use internet sources to analyse the concept of “Ujamaa villages”.
Use ICT tools to study the history of Asian communities in Uganda.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 6: Separatism and Ethnic Nationalism in Africa

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the turbulent history of Africa by analysing selected case studies of civil wars in Africa to appreciate the need for peaceful coexistence.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the causes and effects of the 1955–1972 and 1983–2005 civil wars in Sudan to appreciate the importance of inclusive government, social cohesion and the value of sharing resources equally. (gs, v, a)
analyse the causes and outcomes of the 1990–94 Rwandan Civil War to promote peace-building initiatives and fight against ethnic divisions. (gs, v, a)
analyse the causes and consequences of the 1960–64 Katanga Secession to understand our own resource sharing-related challenges. (gs, v, a)
Evaluate the causes and the consequences of the Biafran Civil War of 1970 in Nigeria to strengthen the peace-building initiatives among the African states.

suggested_learning_activities.description: In a brainstorming session, learners share on the concept of a civil war and its features, giving relevant examples from African continent.

Learners use textbooks, newspapers, ICT tools and other sources to investigate the causes of the Sudanese Civil War of 1955–1972 and 1983–2005. They present their findings to class, highlighting key issues such as ethnic divisions, political tensions, and resource distribution.
Learners, using textbooks, internet sources and other reading materials, present their evaluations of the war’s impact on both Sudan and South Sudan, discussing socio-economic and political outcomes.
Learners watch a documentary or listen to a narration on the 1990–94 Rwandan Civil War, take notes, and discuss the causes of the civil war.
Learners, in a debate session, discuss the results of 1990–1994 Rwanda Civil War. A panel of teachers do a wrap-up.
In groups, learners discuss socio-economic and political reforms in Rwanda after the civil war. They assess the impact of the reforms on national unity and development.

Learners explore resources, including articles, historical documents and videos, to establish the causes and consequences of the 1960–64 Katanga Secession in Congo. They focus on the political, economic, and social factors.

Learners engage in a discussion on how the Katanga Secession influenced national identity and international relations. They explore lessons learnt from the secession and their relevance to modern governance and unity.
In a think-pair-share session, learners discuss and present the causes of the 1970 Biafran Civil War.
In a debate session, learners discuss the results of the 1970 Biafran Civil War.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learners as they work in a group to generate the causes of the civil war in Sudan from 1955–1972 and 1983–2005 and take a note of their ability to: i) interact with one another. ii) use ICT tools responsibly to generate correct ideas.

Engage learners in a dialogue to assess their ability to organise and analyse the results of the 1990–1994 Rwandan Civil War in Central Africa and take note of their ability to: i) make logical presentations. ii) sort and analyse historical information clearly.
Assess the relevance, accuracy and coherence on the lessons learnt from the Katanga Secession of 1960–1964 by modern African states.

suggested_uses: Use ICT tools to investigate the causes of the Sudanese Civil War.
Use internet sources to present evaluations of the war's impact on Sudan and South Sudan.
Explore resources including videos to establish causes and consequences of the Katanga Secession.

themes.theme_title: Unit 2: History of World Affairs Since 1789

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 3: Post-World War I Ideologies in Europe

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the influence of authoritarianism on the post-World War I period by examining the repressive systems in Europe to appreciate the need to avoid extremism in modern politics

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the causes and outcomes of the 1917 Bolshevik Russian Revolution to understand its impact on global politics. (u, gs, v)
analyse the rise of Nazism in Germany (1933–45) and its impact on Europe to understand its influence on world order. (gs, v, a)
analyse the rise of fascism in Italy from 1922–45 and its impact on Europe to understand its influence on world order. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners use internet sources, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the background of the 1917 Bolshevik Russian Revolution.
Learners, in groups, use various sources to search for the causes and outcomes of the 1917 Bolshevik Russian Revolution.
In a think-pair-share activity, learners analyse the factors that contributed to the success of the 1917 Bolshevik Russian Revolution and share with the class.
Learners, in a debate, discuss the significance of the 1917 Russian Revolution in shaping contemporary political ideologies and social change.
Learners use various sources to search for the concept of Nazism in Germany.
Learners use the internet and textbooks to search for and present the social, economic and political conditions in post-World War I Germany that facilitated the rise of Nazism.
Learners, in groups, discuss the methods used by the Nazis to consolidate their ideology in Germany. The teacher does a wrap-up.
Learners, in groups, read an extract on Adolf Hitler’s career and analyse the factors that led to the collapse of Nazism in Germany.
Learners individually write essays on the impact of Nazism, and analyse the dangers of extremism and authoritarianism in the contemporary world.
In a brainstorming session, learners explore the concept of fascism in Italy. The teacher does a wrap-up.

Learners, in groups, use online sources, textbooks, extracts and other materials to search for the social, economic and political conditions in post-World War I Italy that facilitated the rise of fascism.
Learners, in groups, use textbooks and internet sources to search for the methods used by the fascists to consolidate their ideology in Italy.
Learners, in groups, read an extract on Benito Mussolini’s career, analyse and present the factors that led to the collapse of fascism.
Learners, in groups, discuss and present the impact of fascism in contemporary politics.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they present the causes and outcomes of the 1917 Russian Revolution and focus on their: i) skill to manage goals and time. ii) ability to work effectively in diverse teams.
Engage with learners in a dialogue to assess their ability to identify and analyse the reasons for the emergence of Nazism in Germany (1933–1945).
Evaluate learners’ ability to write accurate and coherent historical accounts of the factors behind the rise of fascism in Italy (1922–1945).

suggested_uses: Use internet sources to search for and present the background of the 1917 Bolshevik Russian Revolution.
Use the internet to search for the social, economic and political conditions in post-World War I Germany.
Use online sources to search for the social, economic and political conditions in post-World War I Italy.
Use internet sources to search for the methods used by the fascists.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 4: World War II (1939-1945) and Its Aftermath

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the second international conflict by evaluating the causes and effects of World War II to appreciate how the war has shaped world order since 1945.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the causes and results of the 1939–1945 World War II and its relevance to contemporary conflict prevention and international relations. (gs, v, a)
analyse the role of the United Nations since 1945 to understand its effectiveness in promoting global peace, security and cooperation. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the role of the European Economic Community 1953– 1990 (EEC) to appreciate the need for integration and cooperation among nations. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the ideological tensions of the “Cold War” period to understand their impact on global alliances. (gs, v, a)
assess the role of NATO and Warsaw Pact as collective defence organisations to understand their relevance in addressing international conflicts. (gs, v, a)
analyse the role of the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks (SALT) agreement in limiting the production of deadly weapons to appreciate the need for arms control and global security. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners search for the background and the causes of World War II and present to class.
In a brainstorming session, learners share the reasons for the defeat of the Axis powers in World War II, considering factors like strategic errors, resource limitations and strategies.
Learners, in groups, use textbooks and internet sources to search and present on the social, economic and political effects of World War II.
Learners, in groups, compare the causes and outcomes of World War II with those of any current global conflict, analysing similarities and differences.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the background, objectives and achievements of the United Nations since 1945.
Learners, in groups, discuss cases in Africa where the UN has fallen short of expectations and examine the reasons for its shortcomings.
Learners, in groups, analyse the primary objectives of the United Nations Charter and evaluate their significance in the modern global context.
Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the background, objectives and achievements of the European Economic Community (EEC)1953 – 1990.
In a brainstorming session, learners share the challenges the European Economic Community (EEC) faced by 1990.
Learners, in groups, compare the European Economic Community (EEC) and the African Union (AU), focusing on their objectives, achievements and challenges.
Learners brainstorm and explain the meaning of the concept of “Cold War politics” and its features.
Learners work, in groups, to search for and present the key causes and effects of Cold War politics.

Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and discuss the Cold War events like the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Vietnam War and fall of Berlin Wall, examining how they reflect ideological conflicts and their significance for modern geopolitical tensions.

In groups, learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and give a presentation on the formation, objectives and achievements of NATO and discuss how they influenced global issues during the Cold War.

In groups, learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search and present the formation, objectives and achievements of the Warsaw Pact and discuss how it influenced global issues during the Cold War.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the challenges affecting NATO and the Warsaw Pact. The teacher wraps up the lesson.
In groups, learners use the internet, textbooks and extracts to search for the concept of SALT I and SALT II agreements and their objectives.
In a think-pair-share session, learners discuss the challenges and impacts of SALT I and SALT II on global politics.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ ability to use ICT tools effectively as they search for the causes and outcomes of World War II.

Converse with learners as they analyse the achievements of the United Nations Organisation (UNO) and take note of their ability to: i) listen attentively with comprehension. ii) read and write accurate facts.
Assess learners’ ability to present relevant, accurate and coherent historical facts about the impact of the European Economic Community (EEC) on Europe.
Evaluate learners’ ability to analyse the relevance of SALT I and SALT II in achieving their global objectives.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks and internet sources to search and present on the social, economic and political effects of World War II.
Use the internet to search for the background, objectives and achievements of the United Nations.
Use the internet to search for the background, objectives and achievements of the European Economic Community (EEC).
Use the internet to search for Cold War events like the Cuban Missile Crisis.
Use the internet to search for NATO.
Use the internet to search for the Warsaw Pact.
Use the internet to search for SALT I and SALT II agreements.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 7: Nationalisation of Education in Uganda

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates efforts to reform colonial education in Uganda by analysing the different education policies of the Ugandan government since independence to address the needs and aspirations of Ugandans.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the problems of colonial education to appreciate the efforts taken to reform post-independence education systems in Uganda. (gs, v, a)
analyse the role of education in the modernisation of Uganda to appreciate the country’s effort to build a progressive society. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the efforts that have been taken to Africanise the curriculum to appreciate efforts to align education with the country’s development agenda and the global job market demands. (v, a)
evaluate one of the education policies in Uganda to appreciate how it has addressed education needs of the country. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the development of tertiary education in Uganda to understand its impact on the country’s socio-economic development. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, in a brainstorming session, discuss and present features of colonial education in Uganda.
Learners, in small groups, use the internet, textbooks and other sources to find out the challenges of colonial education in Uganda.
Learners, in groups, using the extract about the 1992 Education White Paper in Uganda, read and analyse its recommendations on how to reform colonial education.
Learners, in groups, conduct a field study in their local community to investigate how access to education has improved people’s lives. They write a report for a gallery walk presentation.
Learners, in pairs, discuss the concept of “Africanising the curriculum” and present their findings to class.
Learners, in groups, use media articles, documentaries or the internet to find out about curriculum reforms in Uganda. They write a report and present to class.
Learners, in groups, visit a local school implementing Universal Secondary Education (USE), interview stakeholders and report on its benefits and challenges.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the role of technical and university education in Uganda.
Learners compare Uganda’s technical and university education systems with those of Belgium, focusing on lessons Uganda can learn from them.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners during a discussion on the problems of colonial education and assess their ability to: i) collaborate effectively with peers in a diverse group setting. ii) respect and consider different perspectives during the discussion.

Engage with learners as they discuss how access to education has improved people’s lives and take note of the following: i) How they sort and analyse information. ii) The clarity and coherence of their expression. iii) Their ability to write and present ideas clearly and logically.
Assess the relevance, accuracy and coherence of learners’ facts on the steps being taken to Africanise the Ugandan curriculum.
Assess learners’ ability to work individually or collaboratively in identifying the roles of SADC in the development of southern African states.

suggested_uses: Use the internet to find out the challenges of colonial education in Uganda.
Use media articles, documentaries or the internet to find out about curriculum reforms in Uganda.
Use the internet to search for and present the role of technical and university education in Uganda.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 8: Challenges to Africa’s Growth and Development

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of Africa’s current position in terms of development by examining the key challenges facing the continent since independence to contribute to solutions to these challenges.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the reasons for Africa’s huge debt burden as well as its effects to understand its impact on Africa’s development. (gs, v, a)
investigate the reasons for the prevalence of corruption in Africa as well as its effects on Africa’s development so as to be able to build an honest, transparent and accountable society. (gs, v, a)
analyse the causes and effects of unemployment in Africa to understand how to live an independent self-sustaining life. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, in groups, use the internet, textbooks or other sources to find out about the concept of debt burden and its causes in Africa.
Learners, in a brainstorming session, discuss and present facts on how the debt burden is used as a neo-colonial tool to influence governance and economic policies in Africa.
In a debate session, learners discuss the impact of the debt burden on national development of African states

Learners, in groups, use an extract from the World Bank or International Monetary Fund to discuss and present the historical implications of the debt burden on social services, governance and economic self-reliance.

Learners, in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present historical factors contributing to Uganda’s rising debt burden. Examples are: i) post-colonial economic policies: how early policies laid the groundwork for dependency. ii) Corruption: how corrupt practices undermined financial management during and after colonial rule. iii) Global economic influences: how historical economic conditions, such as commodity price changes and inflation, have increased the debt burden.
Learners, in pairs, use the internet and textbooks to find out the challenges African countries face due to the huge debt burden.
Learners, in groups, use the internet and other materials to search for and present the forms, causes and impacts of corruption in Uganda’s history.

Learners, in groups, are guided in producing a classroom journal on corruption in Uganda, highlighting: i) historical reflections on corruption and its persistence. ii) making a list of the most corrupt organisations and government parastatals. iii) proposals for reducing corruption based on lessons from the history of Uganda.

Learners, in small groups, write an essay analysing the historical importance of transparency, accountability and ethical behaviour in addressing corruption and building a sustainable future for Uganda.
Learners, in a think-pair-share session, discuss and present factors hindering the success of anti-corruption measures in Uganda.
Learners, in groups, find out the causes and effects of unemployment in Uganda.
Learners, in groups, use textbooks and internet sources to develop programmes aimed at reducing unemployment in Uganda with purposeful strategies.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss how the debt burden has caused neo-colonialism and take note of the following abilities: i) Managing time and goals. ii) Recognising the need to consult others.
Converse with learners on the challenges hindering anti-corruption measures in Uganda and take note of their ability to: i) listen attentively with comprehension. ii) work effectively in teams.
Evaluate the relevance and accuracy of factors presented as solutions to unemployment in Uganda.

suggested_uses: Use the internet to find out about the concept of debt burden and its causes in Africa.
Use the internet to search for and present the forms, causes and impacts of corruption in Uganda’s history.
Use internet sources to develop programmes aimed at reducing unemployment in Uganda.

themes.theme_title: Unit 2: History of World Affairs Since 1789

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 5: Nationalism and Challenges of Integration in the Middle East

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses how marginalisation in the allocation and use of resources can lead to the rise of discontent by examining nationalism and the challenges of integration in the Middle East to appreciate the need for equity.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the rise of Arab nationalism and its efforts towards unity to appreciate the relevance of the current Middle East issues. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the impact of the discovery of oil in the Middle East to appreciate its influence on global energy markets and international relations. (gs, v, a)
analyse the impact of the formation of the United Arab Republic (UAR) to understand the search for unity worldwide. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the relationship between the Middle East and the Western world to understand its influence on contemporary global diplomacy. (gs, v, a)
evaluate the causes and impact of the instabilities in the Middle East between 1973 and 2003 to understand their influence on regional development. (gs, v, a)
analyse the relations between Palestine and Israel (1948–1978) to understand their impact on regional stability and international diplomacy. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to investigate and present the meaning of Arab nationalism, its origins, and its composition in the Middle East.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to analyse the causes of the rise and results of Arab nationalism.
Learners use the internet and textbooks to search for and discuss the socio-economic and political benefits of Arab unity with the class.
Learners read an extract on the Arab League, identify the challenges to integration that hindered their unity.

Learners use an extract on the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to research and present the top oil-producing countries in the Middle East, and create a labelled map showing production statistics and key oilfields.
In a think-pair-share session, learners discuss the impact of the oil industry in the Middle East in both the short and long term.
Learners listen to a guest speaker or read an extract about the oil industry in the Middle East and explore how oil wealth has shaped the region’s role in international relations.

Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to search for and present the background and origins of the United Arab Republic (UAR) and create a timeline of key events from its formation in 1958 to its collapse in 1961.
Learners read and analyse documents related to the UAR, identifying the reasons for its formation and the factors that led to its collapse.
Learners, in pairs, use the internet, textbooks and extracts to search for and present the reasons behind Western countries’ involvement in the Middle East.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to investigate the consequences of Western military and political interventions in the Middle East.
In groups, learners brainstorm the major political and economic problems affecting the Middle East, take notes, and then the teacher provides a wrap-up.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to investigate the main causes (roots) of political and economic problems in the Middle East.
Learners, in groups, use the internet and other sources to search for potential solutions to the political and economic challenges in the Middle East.
Learners in a learning station session, explore available sources to investigate the events leading to the creation of Israel and create a detailed timeline of its key developments.
In groups, learners use the internet and other sources to search for the reasons for the partition of Palestine into Palestine and Israel.
Learners, in small groups, discuss and present to the class the effects of the partition of Palestine into Palestine and Israel.
Learners use the internet, textbooks, extracts and other sources to explore the consequences of the creation of Israel on the Palestinian land.
In groups, learners use the internet, textbooks or extracts to search for the Arab-Israeli Wars between 1948 and 1978, and analyse their consequences for the region.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ comprehension and critical thinking skills as they explain the factors behind the rise of Arab nationalism.

Engage with learners as they discuss the long-term impact of oil discoveries in the Middle East and assess their ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams. ii) suggest and develop new solutions.
Evaluate learners’ ability to draw a relevant and accurate map of the Middle East highlighting key oilfields and their production statistics.
Assess learners’ ability to write accurately and present coherently the impact of the state of Israel.

suggested_uses: Use the internet to investigate Arab nationalism.
Use the internet to search for the socio-economic and political benefits of Arab unity.
Use the internet to search for the background and origins of the UAR.
Use the internet to search for potential solutions to the political and economic challenges in the Middle East.
Use the internet to search for the Arab-Israeli Wars.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Topic 6: Developments in Southern Asia and the Far East Since 1939

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of global affairs by examining the political developments in Southern Asia and the Far East since 1939 to appreciate their impact on regional development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the impact of World War II conferences on Southern Asia to understand their influence on regional relations and geopolitics. (gs, v, a)
analyse the collapse of the Kuomintang government in China to understand the challenges of nation-building. (gs, v, a)
examine the causes and results of the rise of communism in China to appreciate the role of ideologies in spurring development. (gs, v, a)
analyse the division of Korea and its impact to understand its influence on regional security and international relations. (gs, v, a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners read excerpts on major World War II conferences to find out their background and objectives. Such conferences include: the Atlantic Charter (1941), the Casablanca Conference (1943), the Tehran Conference (November 1943), the Yalta Conference (February 1945) and the Potsdam Conference (July 1945).
Learners, in groups, discuss the terms of the World War II conferences.
In groups, learners use the internet or other sources to find out the significance of World War II conferences for Southern Asia.
In groups, learners use the internet, textbooks or other sources to find out the socio-economic record of the Kuomintang in China.
Learners, in groups, use textbooks and other sources to find out the factors for the rise and fall of Kuomintang rule in China in 1949.
Learners, in groups, discuss the causes and effects of the rise of communism in China and take notes.
Learners use the internet and textbooks to search for the reasons for the success of the Communist Revolution in China.
In groups, learners search the internet and textbooks to find out the background and contribution of Mao Tse-tung in China.
Learners, in groups, discuss the problems of China’s foreign policy and write a report.
Learners, in groups, engage in a debate on the leadership of Mao Tse-tung in China.
Learners use the internet and textbooks to search for and present the historical background of Korea’s division and analyse the reasons for this geopolitical division.
Learners conduct a search using the internet and other sources to explore the impact of Korea’s partition on the Korean Peninsula and international relations.
In groups, learners read a historical extract on the Korean War (1950–1953) to analyse its causes and impact on the Korean Peninsula.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss the post-World War II conferences to assess their understanding of the background and objectives of these conferences, and take note of their comprehension and listening skills.

Engage in dialogue with learners to assess their ability to analyse the reasons for the rise of the Kuomintang and communist governments in China, and evaluate their level of sorting and analysing information.
Evaluate learners’ ability to provide accurate and coherent explanations of the factors that led to the partition of Korea in 1948.

suggested_uses: Use the internet to find out the significance of World War II conferences.
Use the internet to find out the socio-economic record of the Kuomintang.
Use the internet to search for the reasons for the success of the Communist Revolution in China.
Use the internet to search for the background and contribution of Mao Tse-tung.
Use the internet to search for the historical background of Korea’s division.
Use the internet to explore the impact of Korea’s partition.
